independent_computation.scope_limitation: The scenario's roster/loadout/level configuration lives in scripts/ (golden_snapshot.py), which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from reading, and it is not mirrored anywhere under data/ (grep for 'mandate_abyssal', 'coupled_scenarios', 'health_damage' over the export returns nothing). The ABSOLUTE number therefore cannot be re-derived from the permitted evidence. What IS fully determined by the permitted evidence is the amplifier algebra that maps the participant's incoming damage to health_damage, and that algebra decides which of the two candidate values can be correct.

rule_derived_from_sources.abyssal_unmake: A damage-TAKEN amplifier of +12% that applies to the MAGIC portion only. S1 and S2 agree; 'from all sources' in S1 quantifies the damage DEALER (any attacker, not just the Abyssal holder), not the damage TYPE -- S2 makes that unambiguous: 'take 12% more magic damage'. Physical and true damage are untouched. Passive is unique (S1: unique:true), so it does not self-stack.
rule_derived_from_sources.imperial_mandate_command: A damage-TAKEN amplifier of +7% on ALL damage types, gated on an immobilize and lasting 4 s (S3, S4).
rule_derived_from_sources.composition_on_health_damage: By S6/S7 the survival walk's health_damage is linear in each post-mitigation packet, so any amplifier set acts as a single weighted multiplier on the pre-amp packet stream: health_damage = B * (1 + 0.07*s_vuln) * (1 + 0.12*s_magic-ish), with s_* the share of B carried by packets the amp legitimately touches.

step_1_delta.statement: The new value is 7.573% below the old; equivalently the old is 8.193% above the new.

step_2_bound_test_rules_out_a_vulnerable.argument: Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable is a 7% amplifier (S3, S4). Adding or removing it -- in whole or in part, on any subset of packets -- can move health_damage by AT MOST a factor 1.07. The observed factor is 1.08193 > 1.07. Therefore the delta CANNOT be explained by any change to the Mandate mark alone; the 12% Abyssal curse (S1/S2) must be the term that moved.
step_2_bound_test_rules_out_a_vulnerable.conclusion: The moved term is the 12% magic-damage curse, and it moved DOWNWARD (old amplified more than new).

model_A_curse_was_applied_to_every_damag.old_model: health_damage_old = B * 1.12   (12% applied to the participant's whole incoming stream)
model_A_curse_was_applied_to_every_damag.new_model: health_damage_new = B * (1 + 0.12*s), s = magic share of B
model_A_curse_was_applied_to_every_damag.plausibility: An implied 29.3% magic / 70.7% physical+true split of the damage landing on participant[2] is an ordinary roster mix (one mage's burst against an otherwise AD-weighted team).

model_B_both_amps_were_flattened_onto_th.old_model: health_damage_old = 1.19 * (M + P)   (7% and 12% both applied to everything)
model_B_both_amps_were_flattened_onto_th.new_model: health_damage_new = 1.07 * (1.12*M + P)   (7% on all, 12% on magic only)

step_3_the_delta_is_exactly_the_shape_of.shared_conclusion: Every arithmetic reconstruction that reproduces BOTH numbers has the same signature: the old value amplified damage that S1/S2 say Unmake does not touch (non-magic damage), and the new value confines the +12% to the magic portion. The implied magic share (23-29%) is physically sensible in both, so neither reconstruction is strained.

step_4_is_there_any_reading_in_which_the.test: For 3269.6 to be correct, the fix would have had to strip legitimate amplification worth 8.19% of the participant's health damage.
why_it_fails: It cannot be the Mandate mark: 7% is a hard ceiling (step 2).

It cannot be a legitimate widening of Unmake: both independent source texts (Wiki S1 and Riot S2) restrict Unmake to magic damage, and the parsed atom (S5) carries exactly the pair (700 units, 12 percent) with evidence key 'magic damage'. There is no cached text supporting a 12% all-damage curse.

It cannot be a mitigation/penetration effect: Unmake is worded as a damage-taken amplifier, not as magic-resistance shred (the item's OWN 45 MR is a self stat, S: data/items.json 8020.stats), so no armor/MR path can widen it.

Unmake is unique (S1) and the curse is a debuff on the target, so a roster with two Abyssal Masks must not double-amplify either -- another route by which the higher old value could only be an over-application.
step_4_is_there_any_reading_in_which_the.conclusion: No wiki-supported reading makes 3269.6 correct; the excess is over-application of the 12% curse beyond magic damage (or beyond a single application).

verdict_detail.confidence: high on direction and on the rule (two independent cached source texts agree, and the 7% ceiling argument is a hard bound); NOT a bit-exact reproduction of 3022.0 -- the scenario configuration required for that is outside the evidence this runbook permits.
verdict_detail.what_would_upgrade_this_to_bit_exact: The roster/loadout/level tuple for 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' plus participant[2]'s per-source damage split; with those, health_damage = B*(1+0.07*s_vuln)*(1+0.12*s_magic) is a closed form and the leaf can be checked to the 0.1 rounding.
